##Strategy

Let's first find the indefinite integral $\displaystyle\int\sec^2\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,dx\, $.  Then we can use the result to compute the definite integral.

##Finding the indefinite integral

To find $\displaystyle\int\sec^2\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,dx\, $ we can use U-substitution.

If we let $\blueD {u=\dfrac{x}{3}}$, then ${du=\dfrac13 \, dx}$ and $\maroonD{ \,dx=3\, du}$.  

So we have:

$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int\sec^2\left(\blueD{\dfrac{x}{3}}\right)\,\maroonD{dx}\, &=\displaystyle\int\sec^2(\blueD u)\,\maroonD{3\, du}\,\\\\\\\\
&=3\displaystyle\int\sec^2(u)\,du\\\\\\\\
&=3\tan(u)+C\\\\\\\\
&=3\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)+C
\end{align}$

##Evaluating the definite integral

Now let's compute the definite integral:

$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int^{\pi}_{0}\sec^2\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,dx\,  &= 3\tan\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\Bigg|^{\pi}_0\\\\\\\\
&=3\left(\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-\tan(0)\right)\\\\\\\\
&=3(\sqrt{3}-0)\\\\\\\\
&=3\sqrt{3}\end{align}$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
No, we could use U-substitution to calculate the definite integral directly. 

However, with this method, we must be sure to adjust our limits of integration.  

Here, when $\greenD{x=0}\,$, $\greenD{~u=0}~$ and when $~\goldD {x=\pi}\,$, $\goldD{u=\dfrac{\pi}{3}}\,$, so our limits of integration change respectively.

We can substitute to rewrite the definite integral as:

$\displaystyle\int^{\goldD{\pi}}_{\greenD{0}}\sec^2\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)\,dx\,  = \displaystyle\int^{\goldD {{\pi}/{3}}}_{\greenD 0}\sec^2( u)\,{3\, du} $ 

We can now evaluate the definite integral as shown below:

$\begin{align}\displaystyle\int^{ {{\pi}/{3}}}_{ 0}\sec^2( u)\,{3\, du} &=3\displaystyle\int^{{\pi}/{3}}_{0}\sec^2(u)\, du\, \\
\\\\\\
&=3(\tan(u))\Bigg|^{{\pi}/{3}}_0\\\\\\\\
&=3\Big(\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)-\tan(0)\Big) \\\\\\\\
&=3(\sqrt{3}-0)\\\\\\\\
&=3\sqrt{3}
\end{align}$
